full_judgment:
3. Defendant nos. 1-3 (Government) had contested the suit by filing a written statement stating that the plaintiff has neither title to nor possession in the suit land and his predecessor in interest neither purchased nor possessed the suit land, that the Government is the owner of the suit land and it has been correctly recorded in the name of Government in the RoR, that 2.53 decimals of land of plot no. 7364 was recorded in the name of Azizul Huq Bhuiyan and others in pursuance of a decree of Title suit no. 249 of 1975. The Government has leased out the land of plot no. 1805 and rest of the suit land is being settled to landless cultivators. The papers produced by the plaintiff are forged and fraudulent. 

 4. The added defendant nos. 4-7 had filed a written statement denying the plaintiffs title to and possession in some of the suit plots claiming their ownership in those plots. However, ultimately these defendants compromised the suit with the plaintiff and executed a solenama before the trial court. 

 6. The appellate court reversed the findings and decision of the trial court and dismissed the suit with the observation that the plaintiff failed to prove his title deed no. 6870 dated 10.12.1920, that the plaintiff himself and his witnesses failed to prove plaintiffs possession in the suit land, that they even failed to tell the boundaries of the suit land, that P.W.1 himself admitted that he got compensation for acquisition of his 15/20 taluks, that he did not file any rent receipt, that the plaintiff failed to prove his right, title to and possession in the suit land. 

 8. On the other hand, Mr. Golam Mostafa, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the opposite party supports the decision the appellate court. He submits that the taluks were acquisitioned after the promulgation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, that the plaintiff himself admits that the suit lands are sikimi taluk and that his 15/20 taluks were acquisitioned by the Government and he got compensation for the same, that he submitted choice list at the time of acquisition. He further submits that admittedly the suit land is in the name of Government in the ROR as khas lands, that the plaintiff has failed to prove his right, title to and possession in the suit lands, that the appellate court is the last and final court of facts and the decision of an appellate court on facts cannot be interfered with unless there is misreading of evidence or non-consideration of material evidence, that in this case the appellate court correctly considered the material evidence and decided that the plaintiff failed to prove his title to and possession in the suit land and as such the appellate courts judgment is to be upheld.
